title: add-hdrhist-metrics-and-lightweight-tracing-probes-for-kernel-selection-and-batching
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Added low-overhead histogram metrics (HdrHistogram) and optional lightweight tracing probes for kernel selection and batching hot paths. Includes a microbench harness and a CI job to record microbench baselines for regression detection.
description:
Motivation: We need higher-fidelity, low-overhead micrometrics for kernel selection, per-kernel latency distributions, and continuous-batching behaviour without the cost/volume of NVTX+Cupti instrumentation. This PR introduces an in-process, optional sampling/tracing probe plus HdrHistogram-backed per-op histograms that are cheap to update from hot paths. The goal is to make p50/p95/p99/p999 and quantile-aware alerts practical in CI and on dedicated clusters, and to provide an export path for Grafana dashboards and the benchmark-lab ingestion service.

What this change does: 1) Adds a lightweight tracer (runtime::light_probe) that can be enabled at runtime via env var or admin API. It records sparse sampled events (~1%) and tagged metadata (model_id, route, device, kernel_family). 2) Integrates HdrHistogram-based counters for critical runtime hotspots: kernel_selection.latency, kv_cache.lookup.latency, continuous_batch.worker.wait_ms, continuous_batch.coalesced_size. Histograms support aggregation windows and snapshot/export without blocking the hot path. 3) Adds a microbench harness (tools/perf/microbench) that drives focused scenarios (small sequence short-context, long-context, KV heavy) and emits both histogram snapshots and CSV summary that the benchmark-lab accepts. 4) CI: new microbench job that runs the harness on a small GPU instance and stores artifacts; CI baseline comparisons are optional and gated. 5) Observability: exporter to push snapshots to Prometheus via a pushgateway adapter and a JSON export compatible with our internal benchmark-lab ingestion. Also includes a sample Grafana dashboard JSON (dashboards/perf/histogram-kernel-selection.json) and a README describing dashboard panels.

Design notes and tradeoffs: - We intentionally avoid NVTX and CUPTI for the default path because they create heavy volumes and require CUDA tools; the light_probe is lower fidelity but far cheaper and safe for production. - HdrHistogram was chosen for wide dynamic range and cheap non-blocking snapshots; histograms are kept sharded per-thread to avoid contention. - Sampling rate and histogram bucket config are tunable at runtime; defaults are conservative (1% sampling, 3s snapshot window). - Exporters batch snapshots and respect RT deadlines so we don't affect SLOs.

Files changed (high level): tools/perf/microbench/bench_runner.cpp; runtime/metrics/hdr_histogram.h; runtime/metrics/hdr_histogram.cc; runtime/tracing/light_probe.h; runtime/tracing/light_probe.cc; runtime/batching/continuous_batch.cpp (added histogram hooks and sampling points); runtime/kernel/kernel_selector.cpp (additional counters around selection latency and candidate scoring); observability/exporters/pushgateway_adapter.cc; dashboards/perf/histogram-kernel-selection.json; docs/perf/light_probe.md; ci/jobs/microbench.yml; plus small test additions in tests/perf and unit tests for histogram correctness.

Commit summary: - Add HdrHistogram wrapper and unit tests - Introduce runtime::light_probe sampling tracer and runtime flags - Hook histograms into kernel selection, KV cache lookup, and continuous batch hotpath - Microbench harness and CI job - Exporter for pushgateway and benchmark-lab JSON format - Grafana dashboard and docs - Fix race in continuous_batch previously surfaced by microbench

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for histogram correctness and concurrent updates added (tests/perf/hdr_histogram_test.cc). - Microbench runs on CI with mocked small workloads; artifacts uploaded to internal CI storage (link in job). - Manual validation on perf-canary cluster: collected histograms for 24 hours and compared p95/p99 under controlled load; results attached to this PR as artifacts (ci/artifacts/microbench-20260222.tar.gz).

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag disabled by default. 2) Enable light_probe on perf-canary and dedicated staging clusters for 48h, verify no SLO regressions. 3) Enable histogram snapshot export and ingest to benchmark-lab for dashboarding. 4) Ramp to more clusters if metrics show stable behaviour.

Follow-ups: - Add automated alerting rule generation based on histogram baselines (ENG-2011). - Add optional GPU-side kernel occupancy probe that correlates SM occupancy with selection time (future PR).

Links: Linear ENG-1938, benchmark-lab ingestion docs (internal), dashboard JSON attached.

Checklist: - [x] Metrics library and tests - [x] Hotpath hooks added with guards - [x] Microbench harness and CI job - [x] Exporters and dashboard stub - [x] Docs and rollout plan

review_comments: Evan Morales: Can you make the default sampling rate configurable via env var? Also please add a note about metric cardinality in docs.
Priya Shah (author): Added REDWOOD_LIGHT_PROBE_SAMPLING_RATE and documented cardinality. Kept default 1%.
Sofia Chen: The histogram snapshot path may allocate; make sure snapshots are off the hot path.
Priya Shah: Snapshot path now copies thread-local buffers and aggregates off the hot path; added a test to ensure zero allocations under load.
Luca Bianchi: CI job runs are noisy on shared runners, consider a dedicated runner for microbench to reduce variance.
Priya Shah: Agreed, added an optional label to gate on dedicated perf runners; CI will fallback to mocked runner when unavailable.
notes_on_ci_artifacts: Artifacts from CI microbench runs are stored under ci/artifacts/microbench-<date>.tar.gz; includes raw histograms and CSV summaries for ingestion into benchmark-lab.
perf_regression_guardrails: Feature behind REDWOOD_LIGHT_PROBE_ENABLED flag off by default; sampling rate configurable; histograms use per-thread sharding to avoid contention; exporter uses non-blocking batching with deadline enforcement.
qa_notes: QA should enable the feature on a staging cluster, run the microbench scenarios, and verify no increase in 95th/99th latency beyond 5% compared to baseline. Validate dashboard panels show expected quantiles and tags (model_id, device, kernel_family).
author_acknowledgement: I certify that this change has been validated on perf-canary and includes tests/documentation; will monitor after rollout.
